orbitTypes.name: Sun-synchronous
orbitTypes.text: A near-polar orbit that crosses each place at the same local time every day, so lighting is consistent. Covers the whole Earth, including polar ground stations.

sources.source: Computed from altitude by the simulation (about 97–98° in LEO)

orbitTypes.name: Polar
orbitTypes.text: Passes over both poles and covers the whole Earth, but the local time of each pass slowly drifts.

orbitTypes.name: Mid-inclination
orbitTypes.text: Tilted to stay over mid-latitudes, so it passes the target region more often, but it never reaches the poles or polar ground stations.

sources.note: Slightly above the target region's latitude so the region is covered.

altitudeSources.note: 525 km matches the rideshare's fixed orbit.

altitudeSources.source: Representative value for an example project
altitudeSources.note: Rough lifetime of a small satellite at average solar activity; real decay varies a lot with the Sun and the satellite's shape.

groundStations.name: Svalbard, Norway
groundStations.text: Near the North Pole, so a polar or sun-synchronous satellite passes on almost every orbit.

sources.source: Representative value for an example project
sources.note: About 10 passes of 6 minutes per day; costUsd is rent for the whole mission.

groundStations.name: Fairbanks, Alaska
groundStations.text: A high-latitude station that sees most polar passes, close to the target region.

sources.source: Representative value for an example project
sources.note: About 7 passes of 6–7 minutes per day; costUsd is rent for the whole mission.

groundStations.name: Wallops Island, Virginia
groundStations.text: A mid-latitude station: cheaper, but a polar satellite passes only a few times a day.

sources.source: Representative value for an example project
sources.note: About 4 passes per day in a polar orbit, more in a mid-inclination orbit; costUsd is rent for the whole mission.

groundStations.name: Goldstone (DSN)
groundStations.text: Deep-space dish in the Mojave Desert; about 10 h of Moon contact per day.

sources.source: Deep Space Network site locations; contact minutes and rent are our game values (design.md section 10.2)
sources.note: The Moon is above the horizon about 10 hours a day per site; three sites about 120° apart give near-continuous coverage.
